unity-gain is shown in this
slide. It is merely the ampli-
tude of the expression given
in this slide.
It is clear that a very flat
response is obtained indeed.

tion of non-dominant poles

however, as shown next.
Note also that only a

commentary_segments.text: A plot of the gain A1 in unity-gain is shown in this slide. It is merely the amplitude of the expression given in this slide. It is clear that a very flat response is obtained indeed. This is why this combination of non-dominant poles is chosen by many designers. They can go a bit further however, as shown next. Note also that only a fraction of the open-loop GBW is available in closed loop. The −3 dB point now occurs at about 0.3 times the GBW only.
